en: The Dharmamudrā Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha for the Naga King Sāgara, translated by the Tripitaka Master Yijing of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was in the palace of the Naga King Sāgara, together with a great...
The assembly consisted of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, together with a great multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, the Nāga King Sāgara rose from his seat, went forward to prostrate at the Buddha’s feet, and said:
“Is it possible that by receiving and upholding even a small portion of the Dharma, one may obtain great merit?
The Buddha told Sāgara, the Dragon King:

“There are four sublime dharmas; if anyone receives, upholds, reads, recites, and understands their meaning, although the effort expended is slight, the merit obtained is exceedingly great, being no different from the merit of reading and reciting the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the Dharma.”
What are the four? They are:
"All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; all are suffering; all dharmas are without self; and nirvana is bliss. Recite these with mindfulness.

These are called the four sublime dharmas, the inexhaustible dharma-knowledge of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, by which they early realize non-arising and swiftly reach parinirvāṇa. Therefore, you all should constantly recite them."

At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken this Sūtra on the Dharma Seal of the Four Lines, the assembly of śrāvakas and great bodhisattvas, as well as the eight classes of devas, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Seal of the Dharma Spoken by the Buddha for the Nāga King Sāgara.
